To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The use of cone-beam collimation for SPECT improves lesion detectability in the majority of the cases studied; (2) the improvement in lesion detectability is greater in the case of lesions with lower contrast; (3) the improvement in detection is more pronounced in lesions with higher lesion-to-background ratio; and (4) the improvement in detectability is more pronounced in the presence of a larger number of lesions.
